(a) From the transfer function, the steady-state response is
y′(s) = 0.5Y(s)  ...(i)
At t = 0, U′(s) = 4, so from the transfer function,
Y′(s) = -4/(8s + 1)
When s = 0, Y′(0) = -4/(8 × 1) = -0.5
Therefore, from eqn (i), at t = 0, y′(0) = -0.5Y(0)
Since there is no initial condition, we can conclude that y(0) = 0
Therefore, the steady-state response is
y(t) = 0.5 × 4 × e^(-t/8) = 2e^(-t/8)
Hence, the steady-state deviation is
y(0) = 2e^(-0/8) = 2
Thus, the new steady-state deviation is 2 units.
(b) From eqn (i), at t = 10 min, y′(10) = 2.5/8 × 2e^(10/8) = 2.5 × 2.031 = 5.065
Therefore, the output deviation at t = 10 min is 5.065 units.
(c) From eqn (i), 0.5y(t) = 2.5 × 2e^(-t/8) = 5.065
Therefore, y(t) = 10.13e^(-t/8)
Hence, the time at which the output reaches 95% of its final change is
t = -8 × ln(0.95) = 8 × 0.0103 = 0.0814 min
